chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no good in the child of fornication, nor in his skin, nor in his hair, nor in his flesh, nor in his blood, nor in anything of him,' meaning the child of fornication.
ai.seo_question: What is the status of the physical body of an illegitimate child according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (a.s.) declares that there is no good in the illegitimate child (walad al-zina), extending this lack of goodness to all physical components of the child, including skin, hair, flesh, blood, and everything else. This hadith from Thawab al-Amal highlights the comprehensive nature of the child's status, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the physical essence of the child inherits the spiritual and social consequences of the act of zina. It underscores the idea that the child is a living testament to the sin, affecting their entire being.
